records.text: Ambo Cash is a 7th Legion officer at Wintergarde Mausoleum, coordinating Dragonblight's offensive while worried about his soldiers. He sends help to recover scattered munitions after a frostwyrm attack, use chain guns to cover injured troops, and search the crypts for his missing rogue Plunderbeard. His clipped, urgent orders reflect the pressure of the Scourge assault.
A riding horse.
A corrupted rager, a creature of Dragonblight that corrodes the armor of those it fights.
An Arctic Cloud is a gas cloud found in Dragonblight and the Storm Peaks.
A Kor'kron riding wolf.

Saurfang the Younger prepares the Kor'kron Vanguard for battle at the Wrathgate alongside Highlord Fordragon. He honors proven dedication and takes his father's judgment seriously; his father has entrusted him with battle armor and an axe. Eager to end the Lich King's tyranny, he first insists on Alexstrasza's permission before an assault on the dragons' dying grounds and on stopping the frost wyrm attacks that threaten his forces.
Frozen Elementals are elemental creatures found across several Northrend regions, including the Borean Tundra and Dragonblight. They hurl ice spikes at anything that comes within 30 yards.

Wartook Iceborn is a taunka leader waiting at the Transborea crossing into Dragonblight, where evacuees are sent after the perilous journey across the tundra. He warns that the Scourge's influence is raising dead taunka to attack caravans. He also points visitors toward Emissary Brighthoof, whom he calls kind and says the refugees have accepted as a village elder. When told Icemist is gone, Wartook looks grim.

The Taunka'le Refugees are survivors at Westwind Refugee Camp whose homes the Scourge destroyed and whose families were slaughtered. They mourn their loss, curse the Scourge, and look to Garrosh Hellscream and the Horde as their hope for safety, crying out the Horde's Victory or death! Emissary Brighthoof has them swear the blood oath of the Horde.

Blood Guard Roh'kill is a Horde guard at Westwind Refugee Camp, still recovering from the Anub'ar ambush on an arms caravan he escorted. He and fellow guard Tor'zin barely survived; their injuries keep them from hunting the attackers, so he asks willing fighters to help restore their lost pride.

Emissary Brighthoof is a Tauren representative at Westwind Refugee Camp who argues that the Horde can save the taunka, whom she describes as battered and near extinction under the Scourge. She works to bring them into the Horde, securing recovered arms and a blood oath, and sees their survival as strengthening the Horde in Northrend.

Blood Guard Tor'zin is a Horde guard at Westwind Refugee Camp and a fellow survivor of the Anub'ar ambush on an arms caravan. Roh'kill recounts that the two barely escaped and were left too injured to hunt the attackers themselves; he identifies Tor'zin as sharing in their effort to recover their lost pride.

A displaced Taunka'le refugee in Dragonblight, mourning the slaughter of their family and the loss of home. They condemn the Scourge and the Lich King's devastation, and see Hellscream and the Horde as their remaining hope.

Elder Ko'nani is the Kalu'ak chieftain in Dragonblight, trying to guide his people through upheaval that threatens their way of life. He seeks help recovering stolen supplies and reluctantly calls for Loguhn's death to interrupt the wolvar attacks. The Kalu'ak are preparing to leave, though Ko'nani says they do not know where they will go.

Loguhn, called the “Render of Flesh,” is the alpha male of the Snowfall Glade wolvar. Elder Ko'nani describes him as a dangerous leader whose death might briefly ease raids on Kalu'ak stores; Ko'nani expects the wolvar to fight over his place afterward.
Snowfall Glade reavers are wolvar found in the glade. They are a fighting group.

Snowfall Glade wolvar are an aggressive group living in the crowded glade north of Moa'ki Harbor. Their raids on the harbor's goods have made them natural enemies of the Tuskarr; in combat they throw spears and use nets.
Snowfall Glade den mothers are powerful wolvar defenders who fly into a frenzy when badly hurt.
Snowfall Glade pups are young wolvar found in the den area. They can be captured for Trapper Mau'i's effort to give the wolvar a chance to survive alongside the Tuskarr.
Snowfall Glade shamans are wolvar spellcasters in the glade. They maintain a Lightning Shield while out of combat.

Trapper Mau'i is a Tuskarr trapper at Moa'ki Harbor who asks for Snowfall Glade pups to be captured. He worries that the wolvar may be slain in the Tuskarr's push to survive, and wants them to have a chance to live alongside his people.

Tua'kea is an old Kalu'ak fisherman and trapper at Moa'ki Harbor. He worries that his ancient aquatic nemesis Tu'u'gwar has returned, and prepares a baited hook to draw the creature out. He relies on others to recover his crab traps and help deal with the threat, and speaks warmly of the Kalu'ak community.
A hostile Surge Needle sorcerer, a spellcaster who hurls arcane blasts. Many sorcerers gather around the Surge Needle, giving the area a distinctly magical threat.
An emaciated male mammoth found in the Borean Tundra. This bull can trample nearby foes, making its bulk dangerous even as its name marks it as starved.
An emaciated mammoth of the Borean Tundra. It can trample nearby foes, a reminder that even this gaunt animal remains physically dangerous.
An emaciated mammoth calf, a young mammoth found in Dragonblight.
A Nexus Guardian found near the Surge Needle in Dragonblight, a magical sentinel that breathes frost.
A bronze shrine warden stationed at a Dragonblight shrine, who blasts intruders with sand and can stop time.
A Dragonblight mage hunter who follows its orders to the letter: it tells an ambassador to wait here, and apologizes that it cannot do otherwise.
A beast found around Moonrest Gardens in Dragonblight that burns the mana of anything that comes close.
An ice revenant found near Dragonblight's shrine area, it attacks with Icy Torrent.
An emberwyrm of the Ruby Dragonshrine, it belongs to ranks that the shrine's defenders fear will grow as fallen red dragons bolster them.
Jotun, the Curse Bearer, is a giant in Dragonblight.
A hostile crystalline ice giant found across several parts of Dragonblight, which hurls ice boulders at those nearby.
A hulking jormungar inhabiting parts of the region, it fights with corrosive poison and may visibly falter, opening its mouth wide.
A magnataur patriarch.
A hostile crystalline ice elemental found in parts of Dragonblight, which slashes at anything close with ice.
An Anub'ar cultist.
A Lothalor Ancient of the Lothalor Woods, one of the ancients that can be strengthened with the Bark of the Walkers. Once strengthened, it gives its thanks and soon disappears.
An arcane wyrm found around the Lothalor Woods and nearby areas of Dragonblight, which channels arcane energy into those near it.
A Lothalor Ancient in the Lothalor Woods, corrupted by arcane wyrms and deadly; it unleashes arcane explosions.
An Indu'le mystic from the village. The blue dragons' magic has brought ruin to the area and left many Kalu'ak dead or driven the survivors insane; the mystic remains dangerous to approach.
An Indu'le fisherman from the village, among the Kalu'ak whose spirits are in danger after the blue dragons' magic devastated the area. Blue radiation surrounds it.
An Indu'le warrior from the village. The blue dragons' magic has devastated the area and put Kalu'ak spirits in danger; this warrior uses Spectral Strike against nearby threats.
Goramosh is a hostile figure tied to the negotiations of the Accord. He says the agreement has been negotiated and only its details remain, then threatens an intruder.
An Ice Heart jormungar feeder, one of the worms attacking the taunka at the Crystal Vice. Ko'char calls for the feeders to be cleared from the canyon.
An Ice Heart jormungar spawn, a worm of the kind found in the Crystal Vice caverns.

Rattlebore is the jormungar spawnmother in the caverns beneath the Crystal Vice. Ko'char says an adventurer from the Plaguelands gave her that name; he describes her as large and fears the threat she poses to his people's hold on the cavern.
A Taunka orphan: a child of the Taunka people.

Arcanimus is a monstrous elemental unleashed when sorcerers bored into the resting place at Moonrest Gardens. It feeds on the spirits of the dead, and Ethenial Moonshadow calls for its destruction. It has an arcane force shield effect while out of combat.

Overlord Agmar commands the Kor'kron from Agmar's Hammer and speaks with emphatic, calculating authority. He directs Roanauk Icemist's formal induction into the Horde and frames the Northrend campaign as a push against the Nerubians and Scourge toward Icecrown. His dealings can be ruthless: he laughs at news of the death of Deino's brother and holds the secret over the one who killed him.
Lak'tuk, called Suffering, is a beast in Dragonblight.
Gar'mak, called Anguish, is a beast in Dragonblight.

Anub'ar Nerubian ambushers are hostile creatures encountered in Dragonblight's woods east of the Westwind Refugee Camp. They rush into combat when provoked, making them part of the threat the Horde is hunting there.
A deranged Indu'le villager of the Indu'le area in Dragonblight, driven insane and hostile, who lashes out in tantrums.
An Anub'ar Nerubian dreadweaver encountered in Dragonblight, this creature holds its ground outside combat and attacks with Shadow Bolt when engaged.

Senior Sergeant Juktok is a Horde officer at Agmar's Hammer, directing the campaign against the Anub'ar and investigating the Nerubians' route from the Pit of Narjun. He sees the escaped taunka as potential allies and backs Lord Hellscream's effort to bring them into the Horde. Juktok speaks in blunt military terms, focused on finding threats and carrying the fight to them.
A tree-like creature found in Dragonblight. Asked for its bark, it may turn angry and attack, or break off a piece, hand it over and depart.
An Arctic Ram is a tundra beast that gores intruders who threaten it.
A Taunka Soldier stands amid the tragedy and chaos at a place that defies the Scourge. His spoken words show pride in being Horde.
Emissary Skyhaven is an emissary in the harbor area who urgently sends visitors to Stars' Rest, where Archmage Modera expects them, warning of upheaval in the land and its wider consequences.
Envoy Ripfang is an envoy in the harbor area who urgently sends visitors to Agmar's Hammer, where Archmage Aethas Sunreaver expects them, warning of upheaval in the land and its wider consequences.

Tariolstrasz is a dragon steward of Wyrmrest Temple, appearing in elven form. He receives letters of introduction for the queen and keeps them safe while directing visitors to consult their ambassador. He can arrange drake rides to the queen's chamber or to Lord Afrasastrasz.
A dragonkin sentinel stationed at Stars' Rest, one of the outpost's watchful guards.
A Moonrest Highborne spellcaster who wields deadly shadow magic, including Shadow Word: Death.
A Winter's Sister who attacks nearby foes with Frost Shock.

Commander Saia Azuresteel serves at Stars' Rest in Dragonblight. A letter reveals that Em, Archmage Malin's daughter, was forced to serve Malygos's army while secretly sabotaging it; this is Em's account, not Saia's. Saia reacts with shock and compassion, promises to send the letter to Malin, and reassures its bearer that they could not have known Em's situation.
Jormungar Tunnelers are burrowing creatures of Dragonblight that attack with Bore and Corrode Flesh.

The Image of Archmage Aethas Sunreaver, bearing the Kirin Tor designation, investigates the redirected ley-line power near Agmar's Hammer. He suspects the mage hunters are changing the energy and worries about what their work means. He explains Northrend's ley lines to mages and connects their attunement to reaching Dalaran; his brisk manner shows in his impatience with delay.

Ko’char welcomes visitors to share the canyon refuge from dragons, but warns that goblins cannot be trusted. He says jormungar have taken to eating his people, and that their cavern cannot be reclaimed until Rattlebore is removed.
Magmawyrm is an undead creature.
A young magnataur.
A magnataur of the camps surrounding Wyrmrest in Dragonblight. Snobolds hide under the magnataur as its slaves, and it will fight on their behalf.
An Arctic grizzly, one of the wildlife of Dragonblight.
A dragonbone condor found across Dragonblight; when badly wounded, it may veer away in an evasive maneuver.

Orphan Matron Twinbreeze cares for orphaned infants and hopes that, with love and affection, they will grow into strong members of the Horde and leave the painful reminders of their shattered lives behind. Her words express a hope for their future, not a promise about any individual child's fate.
A pack kodo of the Taunka.
A Wastes Digger, one of the undead digging around Galakrond's Rest, whose constant presence is a nuisance to the work at Nozzlerust Post.
A Wastes Taskmaster at the digs around Galakrond's Rest, among the undead who are a constant nuisance to the work there.

Wind Trader Mu'fah is an Ethereum representative negotiating an accord with the Blue Dragonflight. He says Malygos personally assured him that Goramosh's commander would prioritize the terms, and grows openly impatient while waiting for Goramosh to finish a ritual. He expects deference, demands immediate escort, and threatens to reconsider the accord.

Ethenial Moonshadow seeks vengeance for the mage hunters' destruction of the resting place at Moonrest Gardens and threatens their base with spirits if they refuse. Ethenial also calls for Arcanimus to be destroyed because it feeds on the dead's spirits, and warns that the Blue Dragonflight's damage to the ley line anchor threatens everyone. Gratitude follows completed requests, but Ethenial insists Arcanimus remains a danger until it is dealt with.

Soar Hawkfury is Agmar's Hammer's stablemaster, whose work reaches beyond the stables: he organizes efforts to address the Scourge's disease among Dragonblight wildlife. He regrets having to cull infected animals and regards it as necessary, then turns to inoculating those that can still be saved. He works with Doctor Sintar Malefious on a vaccine and values the effort to protect the beasts.

Doctor Sintar Malefious, Grand Apothecary at Agmar's Hammer, is developing a vaccine for the region's wildlife. He is sharp-tongued and openly contemptuous of Soar, whom he insults even while settling their debt. Impatient with visitors, he guards some of his work as classified and limits its details to those who need to know.
Jennings is Doctor Malefious' assistant at Agmar's Hammer.
A Forsaken chemist in Dragonblight.
An undead test subject in Dragonblight.
A beast called a Moa'ki Bottom Thresher, found in a small group in Northrend.

Kili'ua, called “Two Huge Pincers,” is described as the mother of all crabs, pacing on an island southwest of Moa'ki. Tua'kea seeks her flesh as bait for Tu'u'gwar, the ancient aquatic nemesis he believes has returned; Kili'ua defends herself with a claw-grasping attack.
Kanosak is Moa'ki's dockmaster and knows of two great sea turtles, Walker of Waves and Green Island, which swim between Unu'pe and Kamagua.

Borus Ironbender is a grand master blacksmithing trainer at Agmar's Hammer. The Wrathgate's living metal fascinates him: he seeks Black Blood samples, then Scourge armaments to study how their metal is forged. He pushes his workers hard for Kor'kron deliveries, threatens to replace them with goblins, and even blusters about beating an orc who slows the work.
Agmar's Siegesmith, a siegesmith in Dragonblight.
Narzun Skybreaker is a wind rider master in Agmar's Hammer who offers air travel. He calls for guards.
Aegalas sells food and drink at Agmar's Hammer in Dragonblight.
Zebu'tan is a troll who sells herbalism and poison supplies, pairing his trade with flirtatious banter. He calls out to an elfy, offers roses, and playfully claims passersby have a crush on him.

Alys Vol'tyr runs the reagents and enchanting supplies stall. She is sharp and openly dismissive: she tells unwelcome admirers to get lost, reacts with disgust, and rejects advances with a firm Never! or the pointed claim that she already has a man.
A Kor'kron war rider, a beast in the Horde's service found around Agmar's Hammer.

Valnok Windrager is the Kor'kron Wing Commander at Agmar's Hammer, coordinating attacks from the air against the Anub'ar threat to the Horde's Wrathgate forces. He gives fighters a flare gun to summon a war rider against the blightbeasts at Icemist Village, and warns that the riders are trained to fight only at Icemist. His salutes and casual hot shot greeting mix military formality with confidence.
A Coldwind Waste Huntress found in the Coldwind area, who pecks at her foes' eyes.

Coldwind Witch is a shared creature type found in the Coldwind area. Coldwind Witches are among the harpies attacking shipments to the gate, while their combat behavior is to cast Coldwind Blast at nearby targets.
The Mistress of the Coldwind is a harpy leader associated with attacks on shipments bound for the gate. She is among the Coldwind harpies targeted in the mountains northwest of Nozzlerust Post.
Quartermaster Gakzug is a quartermaster at Agmar's Hammer who hands out work to visitors.

Koltira Deathweaver is a death knight whose runeblade, Byfrost, thirsts for the Lich King and his minions. He says shadow beings torment him and asks for their defeat; in return, he offers to translate a Scourge tome and seeks sources of frost, blood, and shadow power to etch into his blade.
Bloodmist is Koltira Deathweaver's deathcharger, a named mount associated with him.

Serinar is a black dragon of the brood whose bones the Cult of the Damned exploits at Obsidian Dragonshrine. He despises the cult and shows no mercy, but uses a necrolyte disguise to uncover its purpose. His dry, contemptuous remarks about the cult sit alongside wry surprise that Nalice received aid from an outsider.

Toalu'u is a Kalu'ak mystic troubled by the silence from Indu'le after disaster struck his people. He seeks spiritual guidance through visions, revered elders and the sea-goddess Oacha'noa. He believes all souls share the world's magic and, after hearing Oacha'noa's counsel, says the Kalu'ak must oppose blue dragons trying to control it. He is surprised when an outsider proves a champion of his people.
A Kor'kron Windrager in Dragonblight.

An Anub'ar Underlord is a formidable Anub'ar foe in the Dragonblight. Kilix the Unraveler calls on his allies to fight the Anub'ar forces at the Pit of Narjun and names Underlords among the enemies to defeat. This one warns that a mortal has made a fatal mistake and will not escape.
An Anub'ar Slayer is an undead fighter of the Anub'ar forces, encountered in Dragonblight including around Icemist Village.

An Anub'ar Blightbeast is one of the monsters the Anub'ar are constructing at Icemist Village. Valnok says they plan to send the beasts against Horde soldiers at the Wrathgate and describes them as an aerial force. His mission calls for striking them from a Kor'kron war rider.

Under-King Anub'et'kan is the Anub'ar leader holding High Chief Icemist prisoner. He urges the Taunka to yield to the Scourge, threatens Icemist, and orders his forces to leave no survivors and tear apart the village. When challenged, he calls his opponent insolent and vows they will be consumed; in defeat, he reacts with disbelief. The confrontation centers on Icemist's rescue and Anub'et'kan's defeat.
A young grizzly cub found among the local wild beasts.
A snowshoe hare found in the local wilds across more than one subarea.
A wild elk found across many subareas of the region. When a nearby threat comes within range, it can answer with a Puncture attack.
A blighted elk found among the region’s wild beasts across several subareas of the region.

Captain Gort is a Kor’kron guard captain associated with Agmar’s Hammer. He says he personally witnessed High Cultist Zangus betray the stronghold and lead an Anub’ar assault, and vows to hunt down others like him. Gort’s replies show a blunt, grim manner: after Zangus’s death he says, “I told you we’d get you,” while remembering a fallen mage for his conjured feasts before dismissing him with irritation. His account also treats suspicion as urgent: “kill first, ask questions later.”
A rabid grizzly found among the region’s wild beasts in several subareas.

Narf works at Nozzlerust Post, where he is blunt about protecting the operation and its profits: he sends help against undead and harpies disrupting the work, then brusquely dismisses those who return. He calls Zort his brother, doubts his judgment, and sends helpers to see whether Zort can use a hand negotiating with giants.

Messenger Torvus carries a covert message for Lord Hellscream. He slips a visitor a letter to read and destroy, whispers instructions to play along, then publicly greets them as a soldier and asks them to confirm they accept before he reports back to his lord.

Greatmother Icemist speaks with respect and gratitude to those who helped her people survive, though asking for more help pains her. She is distressed that her only son, Banthok, has left to search for his father, High Chief Icemist, and asks that Banthok be found.

Kilix the Unraveler is a Nerubian survivor of the struggle over Azjol-Nerub, his people's ancestral home. He seeks to reclaim it from the Scourge and the Faceless Ones, whose emergence from the depths helped cost his people their home. His plan to weaken the Faceless Ones is to burn their Watchers' corpses, and he hopes the deeds of those who aid him will restore his people's hope.

Roanauk Icemist, High Chieftain of the Taunka, is held in Icemist's Prison. He grieves over what has been done to his people and pleads to be freed. Once free, his anger turns against his captors; he calls for his brothers to rise and fight again, invoking the ancestors' fury.
High Cultist Zangus is a cult leader whom Warden Jodi Moonsong's vision places in the Pit of Narjun. She identifies him as a target whose death may help end the land's suffering.

Zort is a researcher at the Crystal Vice studying the Jormungar and their attacks on the Ice Giants. After Ko'char refuses to meet with him, Zort hopes evidence about the worms might help win the giant leader’s trust. He investigates their corrosive spit for an elixir, but is also willing to capture and exploit their young when diplomacy fails.

Xink at Nozzlerust Post is a resourceful, profit-minded supplier who equips troops with ore, lumber and Jormungar meat. He provides a controllable shredder for timber work and a replacement device when needed. Xink sees wartime fighting as a chance to make money, and his work is driven as much by the saleable haul as by the troops’ needs.

Zivlix is an inventive but unreliable bomb maker at Nozzlerust Post, trying to finish a flying war machine for sale at the Wrath Gate. He asks for help finding shrapnel materials, changing from ice shards after they melt to bone splinters, and seeking thin hides to package the bombs. He blames Narf for bad advice about the ice.

The Image of Archmage Modera is a Kirin Tor projection working with you from Stars' Rest. She investigates the redirected ley-line energy around Moonrest Gardens and worries about what the mages' use of that power means. She can also help you reach Dalaran after you attune to Northrend's ley lines.
Snowplain Disciples are humanoid fighters of the Dragonblight.
An injured mammoth in the Dragonblight, this animal can still trample when approached closely.

Banthok Icemist is Greatmother Icemist’s son, searching Icemist Village for his captive father, High Chief Icemist. He asks for help recovering three Anub’ar key fragments, then works them into a prison key and urges haste in freeing his father and striking back at the Anub’ar.
Captain Emmy Malin calls on others to keep the enemy away from the focus, and she can cast Surge Needle Beam.

Anok’ra the Manipulator is one of the Anub’ar magi holding a key fragment at Icemist. The magus declares loyalty to its master, names Anub’et’kan as the foe’s coming end, dismisses victory as meaningless, and promises to rise again.

Tivax the Breaker is one of the Anub’ar magi holding a key fragment at Icemist. The magus declares loyalty to its master, names Anub’et’kan as the foe’s coming end, dismisses victory as meaningless, and promises to rise again. In combat it casts Scorch.
Sinok the Shadowrager is an undead who gladly dies for the master and warns that Anub'et'kan will end you. Even in defeat he calls the victory meaningless and vows to rise again, more powerful.
Icemist Warriors are rank-and-file fighters found in numbers among the Dragonblight forces.
A 7th Legion wyrm hunter serving among the Legion's Dragonblight forces, this soldier's named specialty is hunting wyrms.
A 7th Legion cleric serving among the Legion's forces in Dragonblight, this member brings the clerical role to the field.
A ravaged crystalline ice giant.

Roanauk Icemist is the Taunka High Chieftain and is presented as a leader invited to join the Horde. His oath binds him to the Warchief and calls victory or death sacred; he also invokes his Taunka brothers and sisters and their cause.
Lieutenant Ta'zinni is a spellcaster who warns travelers they should not have taken the boat north, and attacks with Frostfire Bolt and Dragon's Breath.
Focus Wizards are spellcasters who channel the Surge Needle Beam.

Magister Keldonus is a mage commander who turned against Agmar’s Horde and joined the Blue Dragonflight’s campaign against magic. He channels ley energy toward the Azure Dragonshrine and reports to a lady he serves, while invoking the might of the Blue when challenged.

Grand Magus Telestra serves Lord Malygos and directs Keldonus in the Blue Dragonflight's campaign against intruders. She praises his progress and orders him to deal with an interruption and bring her an intruder's head as a trophy for her chambers. She regards opposition to the Blue Dragonflight as a transgression and threatens to separate the offender's life energy from the body.

Gigantaur is a magnataur lord wanted by Overlord Agmar for attacks on Horde soldiers and installations in Dragonblight. Agmar’s decree calls him armed and extremely dangerous, and crudely adds “bein’ ugly” to the charges.

Sarendryana is at Stars' Rest, concerned by the blue dragonflight's effects on the Lothalor Ancients. She urges visitors to save those who can be restored, both because it is right and because the ancients may choose to aid the Alliance. She hopes to speak with the saved ancients herself.

Dreadtalon is a named creature wanted for repeated attacks on Horde caravans traveling to and from Venomspite. The wanted notice places its lair on a bluff overlooking the Ruby Dragonshrine, east of Agmar's Hammer, and warns hunters to approach with extreme caution and not alone.
A reanimated frost wyrm of the Dragonblight, an undead wyrm that breathes frost.
Junter Weiss is a bat handler who offers travelers fast air transport. When threatened, he calls for guards and summons an enraged felbat.
Numo Spiritbreeze is a wind rider master who offers travelers fast air transport. When threatened, Numo calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
Nethestrasz is a named Flight Master who provides travelers with air transport.

Earthwarden Grife is a Horde-aligned earthwarden at Agmar’s Hammer, where he works to protect the Lothalor Ancients. He distrusts the Forsaken apothecaries and watches their work, fearing its unnatural effects and lack of honor. He hopes the rescued ancients will ally with the Horde, or at least spare those who helped them.
Sarathstra is a Scourge frostwyrm whose frozen heart is sought after its defeat. The dragon hunters have struggled to stop it, and Rokhan can call it down for a fight.

Rokhan is a Darkspear dragon hunter at Dragon’s Fall, where he faces the Scourge frostwyrm Sarathstra. He speaks in a Darkspear troll manner and can call the dragon down, though he admits his hunters are dead or frozen and asks whether you still want to help. He warns travelers about the dangerous western wastes.
Darkspear Dragon Hunters are Horde-aligned dragon hunters found at Dragon’s Fall in the Dragonblight.

Mage-Commander Evenstar was the commander of the mage hunter forces at Indu'le. His corpse and the fallen forces around him suggest elementals rising from the lake bed attacked them after they summoned the ley-line focus.
Derek Rammel is a named Gryphon Master associated with Dragonblight. His travel interaction offers fast travel, and he calls for guards when attacked.

Rodney Wells is a named Gryphon Master. He offers a fast gryphon to Stars’ Rest when the traveler is ready, and his response to a mission warns against another Sundering and says he will help. This presents him as supportive of the effort to address the magical disturbance.

Palena Silvercloud is the hippogryph master at Stars' Rest. She treats an Alliance missive for High Commander Halford Wyrmbane as urgent, offering her fastest hippogryph, Snowstorm, for the journey to Wintergarde. When threatened, she calls for guards.

A goblin supply runner heading east toward the Wrath Gate, he carried explosives bound for Xink at Nozzlerust Post. Harpies killed him in the Dragonblight wastes; his pack was left behind for the journey back to the sender.
Troz is a merchant who sells goods and offers repairs. He boasts that, with enough money, he could take over the world, giving his trading a grand ambition.

Alexstrasza is the Queen of the Dragons at Wyrmrest Temple. She speaks with authority about the Scourge threat to Galakrond’s remains and opposes Malygos’s assault on the temple. She supports mortals with counsel and blessings, but is candid about her limits: she cannot remove undeath’s plague without affecting the body, even when trying to save Bridenbrad.
A Wyrmrest Temple drake is a dragonkin combatant that uses Flame Breath in battle.
Duke Vallenhal is a death knight of Arthas, titled Servant of the Lich King. Koltira Deathweaver sends fighters to confront him at the Ruby Dragonshrine and draw off his unholy energy with a gem.
Wyrmrest Guardians are high-ranking dragonkin found in two areas of Dragonblight. They breathe flame in battle.
Decrepit Necromancers are undead humanoids in Dragonblight. They hurl Shadow Bolts and wield a Conversion Beam, and channel a Necrotic Purple Beam when not fighting.
Battered Drakkari Berserkers are Drakkari fighters found in Dragonblight.
Reanimated Drakkari Tribesmen are undead Drakkari humanoids found in Dragonblight. They cannibalize in battle.
Hulking Atrocities are undead creatures whose bite spreads infection.

Torastrasza is the Red Dragonflight’s majordomo to the Ruling Council at Wyrmrest Temple. Alexstrasza identifies her as her majordomo and directs heroes to speak with her in connection with the Scourge threat at Galakrond’s Rest. Torastrasza offers to arrange drake transport within the temple, including to the ground or to Lord Afrasastrasz.
Tormented Drakkari fight with a roar and a kick; badly hurt, they turn to cannibalism and grow crazed with hunger.
Shadowy Tormentors are demons of the world of shadows that assault Koltira Deathweaver from beyond.

Warden Jodi Moonsong serves at Stars' Rest and speaks of Elune as the goddess whose power can cleanse the moonwell's liquid fire. She believes the Scourge's advance into Icemist corrupts local wildlife, and traces the blight to Anub'ar cultists whose fumes poison their surroundings. Jodi says she has dreamed of High Cultist Zangus and interprets the vision as guidance to find him in the Pit of Narjun; she urges action to end the land's suffering.

Duane is stationed with the 7th Legion at its Dragonblight front, where snobolds have repeatedly plagued the camp and stolen supplies while the soldiers contend with dragons. Frustrated by the attacks, he directs the fight against snobolds sheltering near magnataur and sends help after another raiding band and its leader, Chilltusk. Duane calls a dragon hunt thrilling and hopes the snobold threat will be settled so the Legion can turn its attention back to the dragon menace.

Kontokanis is a Darkspear stationed at Dragon's Fall. During the dragon attacks, snobolds raided the camp and stole supplies; he sends help to kill snobolds hiding near magnataur and pursue another band down the canyon to confront its leader, Icefist. He speaks in a Darkspear-influenced dialect and looks forward to the Darkspear turning their attention back to the dragon menace. His blunt line that a person is not a real mon until they have killed a dragon reflects the danger facing the camp.

Aurastrasza is a dragonkin at Wyrmrest Temple who investigates the magnataur threat. After finding signs of coordinated raids, she seeks intelligence from the solitary runemaster Dregmar and trusts his account of Grom'thar. She directs the challenge against the warlord, then turns attention back to the Scourge and blue flight.

Barracks Master Harga runs the barracks as an inn, offering travelers a place to sleep and make it their home. He is protective of his men and blunt about the rules: wake them and he says he will throw you out into the snow himself.

Dregmar Runebrand is a solitary magnataur runemaster with longstanding ties to Dragonblight's powerful magnataur. His speech scorns those who serve the dragons, warns challengers that they face Grom'thar's clans, and gives a challenger directions to summon the warlord.
Icefist is a brutal snobold captor who calls the captives his slaves and greets pursuers as a meal. He holds the canyon south of Dragon's Fall and fights with Ice Slash and Tusk Strike.

Chilltusk is a magnataur who boasts that his slaves brought him a real meal, treating captured people as servants and food. He lurks in the canyon northeast of the 7th Legion Front, where snobolds flee with stolen supplies.
Bonesunder is a magnataur who holds the canyon northwest of the Azure Dragonshrine. Aurastrasza sees in him unusual magnataur organization and suspects they plan to raid a large settlement.
Iceshatter is one of three dominant magnataur Aurastrasza wants put down while she hunts a powerful leader among them. He patrols the northern edge of the Mirror of Dawn.

Bloodfeast is one of three dominant magnataur Aurastrasza wants put down while she hunts a powerful leader among them. He resides in the southeastern Dragon Wastes, just north of the Emerald Dragonshrine.
Drakegore is one of three dominant magnataur Aurastrasza wants put down while she hunts a powerful leader among them. He wanders below the cliffs west of the Bronze Dragonshrine.
Siegesmith Gulda sells blacksmithing supplies and offers repairs.
Tradesman Kontor sells trade supplies.
Afha sells general goods and ammunition.
Apothecary Bressa is a master alchemist who trains others in alchemy.
Harold Haggler sells general goods and ammunition.
Rohesia Werner sells trade supplies.
Mrs. Winterby is an innkeeper in Dragonblight who invites weary visitors to rest and offers lodging and goods.

Hansel Bauer sees to Venomspite's need for new mounts at the high executor's request. He jokes that dreadsteeds grow from the ground, then whispers about horse graveyards, and wants warhorses taken from New Hearthglen. He frets he may have to rustle them up himself.
Apothecary Wormwick is a Master Alchemy Trainer in Dragonblight.
Bradley Towns supplies reagents and enchanting goods in Dragonblight.
Apothecary Rose supplies alchemy and poison goods in Dragonblight.
Lovely Liddia is a mushroom seller in Dragonblight.
Duncan Fallers, a named humanoid in Dragonblight.
Josric Fame is a Grand Master Blacksmithing Trainer.
A Venomspite Deathguard serves as a guard associated with Venomspite.

Drolfy sells alchemy and poison supplies. In a posted bounty, Drolfy reports that Bloodpaw wolvar attacked while traveling with cousins Skrotee and Brote and fears they were caught. Demanding retribution, Drolfy funds a reward through Highlord Leoric Von Zeldig for killing High Shaman Bloodpaw and his followers.
Lexey Brevig sells reagents and enchanting supplies.
Zybarus of Darnassus is a stable master. Speaking of himself in the third person, he thanks a hero wholeheartedly and believes that without their help he would have died or become “one of them.”
Fanny McLumpkins sells general goods and lets visitors browse her wares.
Illusia Lune is an innkeeper who welcomes visitors to Wintergarde, offering her inn as a possible home and goods for browsing.
Trixy Trixerton sells trade supplies.
Ordal McLumpkins sells food and drink.
Master Smith Devin Brevig sells blacksmithing supplies, repairs equipment and has tasks for those who ask.
Doldaen sells general goods, including ammunition.
Naohain is an innkeeper who offers food and the use of his tent for rest. His brief reply, “I... I do not know,” gives him a hesitant note.
Lanus Longleaf supplies herbalism and poison goods.
Modoru supplies reagents and enchanting goods. He takes pride in robes woven by his grandmother Oluba from fine silk on Draenor.
Sentinel Amberline is a bowyer. She huffs with annoyance, glares briefly at Sentinel Sweetspring, then turns away with her nose in the air.

Sentinel Sweetspring is a stable master who jokes suggestively at Sentinel Amberline. She peers at Modoru's robes, then privately mocks them to Naohain and needles Modoru with pointedly sarcastic praise.
Saramer Whitewillow is a supplier of trade goods.

Courier Lanson is a courier carrying a list that must reach Wintergarde Keep. He says an Anub'ar ambush left him surrounded and too badly injured to continue the journey. He also voices contempt for Scourge aberrations.
Kreug Oathbreaker is a Scourge flesh giant known as a Ymirjar Giant Lord. Illusia Lune's posted bounty blames him for the deaths of her husband, children, and the Whisperveils, and demands justice.
Snowpaw is Sentinel Sweetspring's guardian, a named animal who stays close to her; Snowpaw snickers and nuzzles at her ankles.
Overseer Deathgaze is an undead overseer.

High Commander Halford Wyrmbane leads the 7th Legion at Wintergarde Keep as the Scourge lays siege. He urgently directs reports and rescue efforts as the lower village falls and survivors become harder to reach. He sent his demolitionist Slinkin to aid Siege Engineer Quarterflash, prizes the lift in Wintergarde's morale, and urges the forces toward an offensive against Thel'zan.

Commander Lynore Windstryke leads the 7th Legion at Wintergarde Keep. She sees the Scourge as a threat even in the fallen people of Wintergarde, whom she regards as former mortals now driven to destruction. She also treats the Scarlet Onslaught as a dangerous force whose attacks on her soldiers demand a response, while hoping that defeat will make its members question their allegiance. Her thoughts remain with Fordragon and the fight at the Wrathgate; she urges Wintergarde to hold on.

Highlord Leoric Von Zeldig serves with the 7th Legion at Wintergarde Keep. After the necropolis destroyed the mine, he works to account for the slain miners, return their cards to the registry, and bring the grim news to their families. He also administers rewards for local bounties entrusted to him by residents seeking justice or retribution. The struggle at Wintergarde remains tied in his mind to the larger fight at the Wrathgate, where Lord Fordragon depends on their perseverance.

Duke August Foehammer is a 7th Legion officer addressed as the commander at Thorson's Post in Dragonblight. The Alliance directs arriving reinforcements to report to him as its campaign against the Scourge moves east from Wintergarde. His title and named post mark him as a particular military contact.

Vas the Unstable is a 7th Legion member at Wintergarde Keep who serves as a magical contact. He directs travelers toward Archmage Modera in response to a disturbance in the western ley lines, and offers to teleport them to Dalaran to deliver his signet to Archmage Celindra. Vas explains that the Kirin Tor moved Dalaran to Northrend.

Siege Engineer Quarterflash is a 7th Legion engineer at Wintergarde Keep, studying strange ore found in a mine the Scourge now prospects. He built a homing bot to help find the missing agent Slinkin and prepared an ore sample with his analysis for High Commander Halford Wyrmbane. Quarterflash says he fears his haste to recover the ore may have endangered Slinkin, and argues the agent’s death will help defeat the Lich King.
A 7th Legion infantryman serving in the field, who shouts to demoralize foes and lands crushing blows.
A mounted 7th Legion cavalier serving in the field, who fights with Mortal Strike.
A 7th Legion sentinel serving as watchful protection for the legion’s field force.
A 7th Legion battle mage brings spellcraft into the legion’s combat ranks, serving a military role that combines magic and battle.

Chief Plaguebringer Middleton is a blight researcher at Venomspite, developing an inert strain and pairing it with an activating agent to attack the Scourge. He recruits others to gather components and field-test the weapon, meeting the work with gleeful enthusiasm for the destruction it promises.

Caregiver Mumik is a Tuskarr innkeeper who welcomes travelers to rest by the fire, fish-smell and all. Mumik’s greetings also include a wary warning that outsiders do not understand Tuskarr ways and should not stay long. The inn provides lodging and goods.
Mystic Makittuq sells poisons and reagents at Moa’ki Harbor, where travelers can browse her goods.
Moa’ki Warriors are the settlement’s fighting contingent, encountered in numbers at Moa’ki Harbor among the Tuskarr community.
An invisible stalker in Jintha'kalar, Dragonblight.
Qannik is a fishmonger who sells goods to travelers. His role centers on food goods, distinguishing him from the other traders nearby.
Takubvik sells general goods to travelers.
Trapper Tikaani is a stable master who helps travelers stable pets and recover lost companions. His work is focused on the care and return of animal companions.
Imnek sells trade goods to travelers who need materials or supplies for their own trades.
Kuk'uq is a spearcrafter who sells goods and offers equipment repairs. His craft and repair service distinguish him from the other traders in the area.
Skrotee is an enslaved gnome and one of Drolfy’s cousins. Drolfy says Skrotee and Brote were caught after the Bloodpaw wolvar attacked them in the Eldritch Heights.
Brote is an enslaved gnome and one of Drolfy’s cousins. Drolfy says Brote and Skrotee were caught after the Bloodpaw wolvar attacked them in the Eldritch Heights.

An Onslaught Raven Priest serves among the Scarlet Onslaught forces in Dragonblight. One warns that the Grand Admiral watches their dedication and threatens those who neglect their post; another invokes Abbendis’s purges. The priests fight with Raven Flock magic.

An Onslaught Footman is an armed Scarlet Onslaught combatant in Dragonblight who invokes the Light while calling for purification by steel. Footmen fight as part of the Onslaught’s campaign, which Wroth’s wanted notice targets for execution.
An Onslaught Workman is a Scarlet Onslaught laborer in Dragonblight who fights with a chopping strike.

Torturer LeCraft is the Onslaught's torturer, working in the basement of their barracks. Under the branding iron he cracks, pleading for mercy and giving up that the Onslaught knows of stolen armor, weapons and horses, their immunity to the blight, and a spy disguised as one of them.

High General Abbendis presents the Onslaught as powerful and treats an intruder as an unwelcome interruption, impatiently ordering the intrusion dealt with and threatening to show the Onslaught's real power. Abbendis wields Seal of Onslaught and Raging Consecration.

An Onslaught executioner who impatiently awaits a target, calls them an “impure mongrel,” then dismisses their last words and condemns them to burn in hell. The lines give the executioner a cruel, contemptuous manner.
An Onslaught warhorse.
A Forsaken held as a prisoner.
A ghostly captain of the Forgotten Shore, one of the shipwrecked dead who have not realized they died. He fights with Stormhammer.

A Forgotten knight who mourns Prince Arthas's abandonment and the soldiers' losses. He still hopes the prince will lead them to victory, despite the burned ships and their desperate position. His words reflect a stranded soldier's grief and loyalty.

A stranded Forgotten rifleman waiting for Prince Arthas to return. He longs to go home to his wife and children in Ironforge, but fears the soldiers cannot endure the cold much longer. He blames the peasants' slow work and clings to the hope that the prince will lead them home.

Forgotten Peasants are laborers preparing the base for Prince Arthas's return. Their complaints blame beasts burning the ships for delaying the journey home, and they are focused on getting the base ready.

Forgotten Footmen fear they will perish if Prince Arthas does not return. Their words lament that the ships will not be ready before winter and worry that Arthas and Muradin may be in danger after their long absence.
Captain Shely is a captain who skewers foes with Run Through.
Onslaught Deckhands are ship crew who fight with side kicks.

Blacksmith Goodman is a Scarlet Onslaught leader who works the smithy. Compelled by the Rod of Compulsion, he cries that the Onslaught is all lies and that the Scourge and Forsaken are not their enemies.

Lead Cannoneer Zierhut is a Scarlet Onslaught leader overlooking the beach from the southeast ramp. Compelled by the Rod of Compulsion, Zierhut urges others to renounce the Onslaught and accuses the high general and grand admiral of lying.
Stable Master Mercer keeps the Onslaught's stables. Compelled by the Rod of Compulsion, he insults High General Abbendis crudely and accuses Grand Admiral Westwind of selling them out.

Commander Jordan is a Scarlet Onslaught leader at the barracks. Compelled by the Rod of Compulsion, he claims High General Abbendis told him that coming north was a mistake and that the Onslaught is doomed, urging his comrades to lay down their weapons and flee.
Risen Gryphons are undead gryphons.

High Executor Wroth is a ruthless, calculating leader of the Hand of Vengeance, willing to make captives and compromised subordinates expendable. He recalls working as a torturer at King Terenas’s court and greets the Rod of Compulsion with evil anticipation. His dark humor and offer to recruit an adventurer into the order’s ranks reveal both his cruelty and faith in its hierarchy.

Emerald Skytalons are beasts that defend the Emerald Dragonshrine. Ysera, caught in a nightmare, mistakenly told the shrine's defenders to treat everyone outside the green dragonflight as enemies. They strike with their talons.
High Abbot Landgren is a named, high-ranking cleric. His greeting addresses the visitor as “my son” or “my daughter,” lending his manner a pastoral tone.

Bishop Street is a cleric whose speech joins concern for the Light's protection with impatience at interruption: he welcomes a visitor as my child, then rebukes interruptions to our righteous work. He fights with Holy Smite and Power Word: Shield.
A devout bodyguard, a religiously committed protector who lets out a piercing howl in battle. One is heard asking who rang the bell.

Apothecary Vicky Levine is a Royal Apothecary Society member at Venomspite who experiments against the Scarlet Onslaught and New Hearthglen's operations. She has her sister send supplies and takes pride in the Levine family name. Her plans range from blight to starving rats and burning water. A blight experiment goes wrong around junior assistant Schlemiel, but Vicky is then surprised to find the mixture is working. She is an inventive and ruthless campaigner against the Onslaught.

Junior apothecary Schlemiel is Vicky Levine's assistant in the Royal Apothecary Society. When confronted over a failed batch, he protests that he followed instructions precisely. A blight spell then hits him; he yelps and dies. His brief exchange with Vicky presents him as an inexperienced subordinate caught in her hazardous experiments.
A Moa'ki fisherman, this local figure is identified by his community and trade: one of the people who fish among the Moa'ki.
An elemental lasher that rests submerged, hidden among its surroundings.

Nishera tends Ysera's garden at the Emerald Dragonshrine and seeks to restore the shrine's balance amid the Emerald Nightmare's confusion around Ysera. She accepts death and rebirth as part of nature, and warns visitors that the garden can deceive.

Quartermaster Bartlett is a blunt, wry quartermaster at Venomspite, trying to supply the fight against the Scarlet Onslaught while the coffers are empty. He presses recruits to take enemy arms and seek treasure for the war effort, speaking of sacrifice and his own limited capacity to make enough equipment.
A rotting storm giant, a decaying giant creature found among others in the surrounding area.
A villager risen from death, one of several such undead figures found in the surrounding area.
A Snowplain zealot, one of many fervent adherents found in the surrounding area.
A Snowplain shaman, encountered among the Scourge-threatened reaches of eastern Northrend, fights with a Searing Totem.
A Risen Wintergarde Mage is an undead spellcaster associated with Wintergarde's fallen defenders. It is encountered near Wintergarde Keep.
A Risen Wintergarde Defender is one of Wintergarde's fallen defenders returned as undead. It appears in the Wintergarde area and can answer injury with Unwavering Will.
A Reconstructed Frost Wyrm is a powerful undead dragon found near Wintergarde Keep. It breathes frost.
A Dreadbone Invader is a Scourge-aligned undead encountered near Wintergarde Keep. It fights with Soulthirst.
A Mindless Wight is an undead creature encountered near Wintergarde Keep. It attacks at close range with Smash.
The Death Knight Champion is an undead combatant encountered in Dragonblight, using Plague Strike in battle.
The Naxxramas Necrolord is an undead necrolord encountered in Dragonblight, a combatant whose title ties it to Naxxramas.
The Hungering Dead are undead streaming from what remains of Old Wintergarde, covering the outskirts of the Carrion Fields.
A scavenging beast of Dragonblight, the Tundra Scavenger uses a mauling attack in combat.

At Wintergarde Keep, Zelig studies Northrend's past through his scrying orb, believing Arthas's imprint may reveal truths useful against their enemy. Its visions draw him toward Frostmourne's history and the Scarlet Onslaught's designs, though the orb cannot answer every question. He speaks of fate and calls Orik like a brother, grateful that Orik has found hope.
A Wintergarde villager rescued from fear. They thank their rescuer and offer an open shop, while nervously questioning whether a flight is safe.

Inquisitor Hallard is a 7th Legion inquisitor in Wintergarde Keep, investigating a tome written in the language of death by interrogating Mayor Godfrey, now a Scourge agent. He is devout in his faith in the Light and determined to extract information, using threats and force when persuasion fails.

Gryphon Commander Urik is a 7th Legion officer at Wintergarde Keep’s gryphon station. He explains riding in friendly, practical terms and describes Northrend’s gryphons as especially resilient. His work centers on coordinating the keep’s gryphon service.

Durkon is a 7th Legion cavalier at Wintergarde Keep, where he investigates the Scourge threat inside the town crypt. After barely escaping, he asks the High Commander for help and greets the next volunteer with rough humor about needing to be crazy. Faced with a flesh-bound tome, he admits he cannot interpret it and sends it to High Commander Halford Wyrmbane.

Yord "Calamity" Icebeard is a 7th Legion figure at Wintergarde Mausoleum who directs an operation against the Scourge necrolords and their Naxxramas forces. He treats the necrolords as clowns and asks whether they have been taken care of, aiming to give Ambo time to get things situated.

Deathguard Molder is a deathguard at Venomspite trying to destroy the Scarlet Onslaught's ballistae. Frustrated that the apothecaries reserve their blight spreaders for special missions, he turns to bombs taken from Scourge siegesmiths and boasts that this old-style approach may win the high executor's attention. He is pleased to claim the credit, though he concedes others helped.
An Onslaught bloodhound, a beast of the Carrion Fields that mauls its prey.
Onslaught infantry are humanoid soldiers found around the Carrion Fields and nearby Onslaught territory. They press their attack relentlessly.
An Onslaught Scout in Dragonblight who sprints as soon as a fight begins.
An Onslaught Mason stationed in Dragonblight, who fights by sundering armor.

Onslaught Commander Iustus is a Scarlet Onslaught commander whom Wintergarde blames for ambushing and slaying a 7th Legion battalion, and Wintergarde demands justice. He fights with Whirlwind and, when wounded, Bloodthirst.
The Hungering Dead is an undead creature found in Dragonblight.

A Wintergarde villager rescued from danger, this grateful survivor thanks the hero and says their shop will always be open to a friend. During the flight, they worry about the ride and admit they hate heights; their other remarks range from frightened pleas to relief at reaching safety.

Spy Mistress Repine works at Venomspite, seeking intelligence on the Scarlet Onslaught and directing operations against it. She asks for the New Hearthglen daily orders to learn its plans, then sends them to her disguised agent Agent Skully to inform the next phase of the assault. Repine also orders the elimination of captured citizens held by the Onslaught; her instructions combine intelligence gathering with forceful action against the enemy.
A Bloodpaw Marauder is a hostile fighter of the Bloodpaw in the Grizzly Hills area, worked up into a bloodlust even before a fight.
A Bloodpaw Warrior is a hostile melee fighter of the Bloodpaw in the Grizzly Hills area, who mauls its foes.
A Bloodpaw Shaman is a hostile fighter of the Bloodpaw in the Grizzly Hills area, who strikes with Stormstrike.

Orik Trueheart is a paladin of the Argent Crusade at Dawn’s Reach, investigating the restless dead along the Forgotten Shore. He believes the ghosts are former Alliance soldiers and treats their release as a matter of respect and justice. His own connection to the shore is painful: he was a boy in the prince’s fleet, and remembers Arthas abandoning its survivors after ordering the ships burned. Zelig entrusted him with a crystalline orb years ago; Orik now uses it to help the Forgotten see the world through his memories. He also prepares murkweed elixir to let others enter their realm.

Tilda Darathan is a priestess serving with the Argent Crusade at the Dragonblight camp. She recruits able soldiers for the Crusade’s campaign against the Lich King and directs interested recruits to Crusader Valus at Light’s Trust.
A captive of the Scarlet Onslaught, exposed to the blight. The prisoner moans but seems otherwise unaffected.

Agent Skully is a Venomspite spy undercover as an Onslaught caretaker at New Hearthglen, using a shovel to support her disguise. She works discreetly, investigating the Onslaught’s protection and the high abbot’s role, and uses a banshee’s magic mirror to help an infiltrator impersonate a raven priest.
An Argent Crusade rifleman serving in the campaign around New Hearthglen. The rifleman offers fellow soldiers brief words of blessing and has a blunt combat quip about an enemy’s head exploding.

Rothin the Decaying belongs to the Cult of the Damned and, according to Serinar’s task, resurrects black dragons as magmawyrms in the Maw of Neltharion. He treats the ancient wyrms as valuable to his work, reacts with dismay at their loss and threatens anyone who interrupts him. He insists that death only strengthens, without explaining what it strengthens.
A Burning Depths necrolyte of the Cult of the Damned, among those Serinar condemns as a shameful presence outside the Obsidian Dragonshrine. It attacks nearby foes with Destructive Strike.
An Onslaught Raven Archon who stands its ground rather than advance, and calls a Raven Flock when it attacks.
A Burning Depths Necromancer belongs to the Cult of the Damned. Serinar targets these necromancers among the cult’s forces in the Maw of Neltharion.
One of Wintergarde’s trapped townspeople, held in the town square during the Scourge attack. When freed, the villager greets the rescuer as a hero and expresses gratitude.
A hostile skeleton in the Dragonblight, one of the skeletal servants of the necrolytes outside the Obsidian Dragonshrine. It attacks with Smoldering Bones when provoked.
A blacksmith of Wintergarde, found in the town square.
A Smoldering Construct is an undead creature among the Cult atrocities swarming the Maw of Neltharion.
A Smoldering Geist is an undead creature among the Cult atrocities swarming the Maw of Neltharion.
An Onslaught death knight encountered in the Dragonblight, who strikes with Plague Strike.
A vengeful geist among the undead who overran Wintergarde’s town square. Though once one of the town’s living citizens, it is now a Scourge attacker, described as driven to destroy the living.
Deathguard Schneider is a captured Deathguard held in New Hearthglen by the Scarlet Onslaught. When confronted, he responds with a threat to fight, and he asks to be freed.
Senior Scrivener Barriga is a captured scrivener held in New Hearthglen by the Scarlet Onslaught. He anxiously asks to be released and protests that he will write up anyone who means him harm.
Engineer Burke is a captured sanitation engineer held in New Hearthglen by the Scarlet Onslaught. He pleads not to be killed and says he needs to return to Venomspite to finish his shift.

Chancellor Amai is a captured chancellor held in New Hearthglen by the Scarlet Onslaught. Amai says they had just arrived in Venomspite before waking in the cage, and offers to double the captor’s pay to escape.
A Deathbringer Revenant is a hostile revenant found in Dragonblight and Icecrown that can strangulate a foe.
A Forsaken captive in Wintergarde, known only by the fact that he is a prisoner.
A risen Wintergarde miner that lashes out with Puncture Wound when something comes within reach.
A Scourge siegesmith found in Wintergarde, who hurls bombs.

Slinkin the Demo-gnome is a 7th Legion gnome hiding in Wintergarde Mine. In a note, he says Scourge miners are extracting saronite for their war machines and that he has picked out repeated words despite not understanding their language. He observes that they speak "Yogg-Saron" with contempt.

Ceristrasz is a red dragon of the red dragonflight, helping defend the Ruby Dragonshrine. He asks for aid against the Scourge, including restoring his fallen brood through ruby acorns and stopping the necromancers corrupting the shrine. He remembers Dahlia Suntouch's long loyalty, hopes she has found peace, and promises to report the visitors' help to the council. He also expresses gratitude for Ambassador Lauriel's support.

Necrolord Amarion is a Scourge necrolord at the bottom of Wintergarde Crypt, where the remains of dead nobles and dignitaries are raised as servants of the Scourge. His presence at the crypt's heart is the source of an assault from within.
The Shadow of Thel'zan the Duskbringer is an undead in Dragonblight.
A Fordragon stallion, an animal in the Dragonblight area.
A wounded Fordragon soldier in the Dragonblight area.
A Fordragon footman found in Dragonblight.
A Fordragon carpenter in the Dragonblight area.
A Fordragon gryphon rider found in Dragonblight, a mounted humanoid fighter who calls down Stormhammer in battle.
A Ruby Keeper, a fallen red dragon in the Ruby Dragonshrine area whose body can be returned to the earth with a ruby acorn.
A Frigid Abomination Attacker is a Scourge abomination pouring out of the Ruby Dragonshrine into the canyons, where Captain Iskandar's group holds the passes against it.
A Frigid Geist found among the Scourge forces at the Ruby Dragonshrine. It is one of the attackers encountered in the shrine’s defense.
A Fordragon knight stationed around the Fordragon encampment, who rallies the encampment's defenders with a Rallying Cry.
A Fordragon peasant found at the encampment, among its civilian population.
A Fordragon lumberjack at the encampment, identified by the work of cutting and supplying timber.
A Fordragon mason at the encampment, identified by work in stone construction.

A necromancer of the Cult of the Damned serving among the forces at the Ruby Dragonshrine. It boasts that fallen warriors will swell its army, urges the dead to rise, and declares that the age of dragons is over. Its words frame the shrine’s defenders and dragons as enemies in a struggle it expects to win.
Fordragon Marksmen are combatants in the Fordragon forces.
Ruby Watchers are hostile dragonkin that blast nearby targets with Ruby Blast.
Fordragon Medics serve a medical role among the Fordragon forces.
Stormwind Captains serve the Stormwind forces.
Enraged Apparitions are hostile spirits that fly into a frenzy in battle.
Reanimated Nobles are hostile undead that fight on with Sanguine Strike when badly wounded.
Kor'kron Vanguards are combatants serving the Kor'kron.
Warsong Elites are high-ranking combatants among the Warsong forces.
Warsong Peons are lower-ranking members of the Warsong forces.
A Darkspear fighter who specializes in throwing spears.
An Alliance conscript serving as a foot soldier. They shoot at distant enemies and answer close threats with a Heroic Strike.
Captain Iskandar leads a group of fighters stemming the flow of Scourge into the canyons. He cleaves and whirls through foes and strikes with Mortal Strike.
A Taunka windfury who uses Moonfire against foes and Healing Touch when an ally is badly hurt.
A Taunka huntsman, identified by a hunting role among the Taunka.
A war kodo.

Lord Afrasastrasz was appointed by Queen Alexstrasza to command Wyrmrest Temple’s defenses. He abhors the loss of any life, yet refuses to stand aside while Malygos’s empowered blue dragons threaten the temple. He appeals for help against the attackers and the ley-line power strengthening them, and directs travelers between the temple and the ground.
Fordragon Sentinels are guards who hold their position and keep a defensive stance when not fighting.

Mayor Godfrey resists an interrogator, then under pressure describes a prophecy of apocalypse. He claims Thel’zan the Duskbringer is a human turned lich, protected by the Lich King, and directs attacks from a mausoleum beneath Wintergarde Village. Godfrey warns that Thel’zan cannot be stopped.

A necrolord of the Cult of the Damned stationed at Angrathar, among the Scourge forces gathered in the Dragonblight. A hardened fighter, it holds its ground rather than advance and fights for the Scourge.
A frail construct among the Scourge forces at Angrathar. Despite its fragile appearance, it is a powerful combatant, built for battle rather than conversation.
A colossal abomination among the Scourge forces at Angrathar. It is an aggressive combatant, a hulking weapon of the Scourge.

An azure dragon of the blue dragonflight, emboldened by the excess magic flowing through the Azure Dragonshrine. The flight has attacked Wyrmrest Temple, and these dragons are among the threats the temple's defenders are fighting in the Dragonblight.
A plague eruptor among the Scourge forces at Angrathar. This dangerous creature attacks with a cloud of plague, making it a threat on the battlefield.
Wyrmrest Defenders are dragonkin who can carry a rider into the fight. One says it can't believe the blues would attack them and wants to give some of it back; another speaks of casting renew.
Angrathar Aberrations are undead creatures encountered in the Angrathar area. In battle they cast Lapsing Dream and become enraged.
Wintergarde Gryphons are gryphons found in the Wintergarde area.
Kor'kron Pillagers are humanoid raiders encountered around Angrathar.
Fordragon Armored Gryphons are gryphons bearing the Fordragon designation, found in the Dragonblight region.
Fordragon Stormtroopers are humanoid combatants encountered in the Angrathar area.
A high priest stationed in the Ruby Dragonshrine area, serving as one of the shrine's priestly figures.
A Warsong shaman found in the Ruby Dragonshrine area.

Dahlia Suntouch is identified by Ceristrasz as the Ruby Dragonshrine's keeper. During the Scourge attack she is reported missing; Ceristrasz asks for help against the necromancers and corruption threatening the shrine.

An Azure Drake of the blue dragonflight, among the forces attacking Wyrmrest Temple amid the surge of magic at the Azure Dragonshrine. Wyrmrest's defenders are tasked with fighting the drakes and destabilizing the shrine's ley-line eruption.
A Frigid Geist serving among the Scourge attackers around the Ruby Dragonshrine. Captain Iskandar's defense force is fighting these attackers in the canyons.
A Frigid Necromancer aligned with the Cult of the Damned and present among the Scourge attackers at the Ruby Dragonshrine.
A frenzied gargoyle that uses Gargoyle Strike when it enters combat.
A reconstructed wyrm that patrols a set route, strafing what lies below with frost breath.
A Fordragon battle mage deployed in the fighting around the Wrathgate.
A mindless ghoul encountered in Dragonblight.

A 7th Legion soldier fighting at the Wrathgate. In the battle, one worries aloud about reaching Wintergarde and asks whether stopping the enemy will secure victory; another asks a passerby what they want.
A dragonkin guardian of the Ruby Dragonshrine that cleaves through foes.
A Horde conscript in Dragonblight, this humanoid attacks from range with Shoot and uses Heroic Strike at close quarters.
Rustler Burnhoof is a humanoid found in Dragonblight.
Captain Drayzen leads a group holding the canyons against the Scourge spilling from the shrine; Vargastrasz asks others to aid his defense and stay behind his men. He cleaves and whirls through foes.
The Fordragon Battle Steed is a beast found in Dragonblight.

High Shaman Bloodpaw is a wolvar of the Bloodpaw tribe in Dragonblight's Eldritch Heights. Drolfy's posted account says a Bloodpaw band attacked him and his cousins, and names the shaman and his cronies as the bounty's targets. Bloodpaw uses Lightning Bolt when attacked and remains still out of combat.

Vargastrasz is a red dragon defending the Ruby Dragonshrine as the Scourge turns fallen red wyrms into emberwyrms. He asks visitors to aid Captain Drayzen, restore fallen dragons with ruby acorns, and stop the necromancers and corruption beneath the shrine. Dahlia Suntouch's corruption alarms him; he thanks Horde visitors for aiding his kind and says he will report their help to the council.

Nalice, ambassador of the Black Dragonflight, mocks the red flight's appeals to virtue and treats the Scourge crisis as an opportunity for slaughter. She directs visitors toward Serinar at the Obsidian Dragonshrine, then complains when he misses the battle. She expects other dragons to fear a Black Dragon and scorns the ancient virtues that keep them from attacking her.
An undead image of Razuvious in Dragonblight.
An undead image of Anub'rekhan in Dragonblight.
An undead image of Noth in Dragonblight.

Commander Eligor Dawnbringer gives detailed, orderly accounts of Naxxramas and its Scourge, explaining their histories, powers, and tactics. His separate reflection on Abbendis carries regret, and he voices concern that Barean Westwind has survived, revealing a personal stake in the threats he describes.

Lord Itharius, ambassador of the Green Dragonflight, tests whether the Emerald Dragonshrine's natural properties can aid the fight against the Scourge. He sends someone to gather lasher seeds, then to use them to weaken three specific Scourge threats. He means to take the results to Ysera and urgently wants answers; he says she remains caught in a nightmare and may need coaxing.
The Venomspite Riding Bat is a riding creature associated with Venomspite.
Ysera, known as The Dreamer, is a dragonkin.
A 7th Legion Rifleman is one of the Legion’s rifle-armed soldiers, firing his weapon in combat.
The Tattered Abomination is a hostile creature in Dragonblight that snags distant foes with a Scourge Hook.
The Scourge Technician is a hostile creature in Dragonblight that Lobotomizes foes at very close range.
The Leprous Servant is a hostile creature in Dragonblight whose Leprous Touch afflicts those within reach.

Lauriel Trueblade is the Alliance ambassador at Wyrmrest Temple. She sees cooperation with the red dragonflight as valuable amid the battles ahead, and has arranged a regiment to help it fight the Scourge at the Ruby Dragonshrine. She also gives visiting Alliance personnel an important task to complete before they meet the red dragon queen.

Golluck Rockfist is the Horde ambassador at Wyrmrest Temple. He presents aid to the red dragonflight as repayment for the Horde's past abuse of Alexstrasza and her kin: he has arranged a regiment to fight the Scourge at the Ruby Dragonshrine. He also gives visiting Horde personnel a task to complete before they meet the red dragon queen.

Necrolord Horus is one of the Scourge necrolords working to empty the crypts beneath Wintergarde Mausoleum. He is a hostile combatant who casts Shadow Bolt when engaged and remains still while out of combat.
Turgid the Vile is a Scourge combatant who spews Vile Vomit and snags distant foes with a Scourge Hook.
An undead Scourge test subject in Dragonblight.
A Naxxramas Dreadguard is a Scourge guard in the mausoleum that attacks with Soulthirst.
A Naxxramas Shade is a Scourge combatant in the mausoleum that strikes with Dark Strike.

Necrolord X'avius is a named Scourge necrolord working with Necrolord Horus to empty the crypts beneath Wintergarde Mausoleum; Wintergarde's expedition targets them before advancing toward Thel'zan. In battle, X'avius uses Shadow Bolt and Shadowflame.

Plunderbeard was Ambo Cash’s rogue, sent to investigate a Scourge tunnel beneath the Wintergarde Mausoleum. His recovered journal describes corpse experiments, bone constructs made from corpses that cannot be reanimated, and his suspicion that Thel’zan may once have been one of them. He had also found the lich’s phylactery before the remaining journal pages were torn out.

Dreadbone Constructs are Scourge bone constructs found around the Wintergarde Mausoleum crypts. Plunderbeard’s recovered journal says corpses that cannot be reanimated are made into bone constructs, connecting these creatures to the mausoleum’s corpse experiments.
Wailing Souls appear in the crypts beneath Wintergarde Mausoleum. They use the spell Tug Soul during combat.

Fenrick Barlowe, an apprentice bat handler, grumbles that awkward approaches leave broken-necked bats and bat gizzards for the gnomes. He blames trees that the unit is not allowed to cut for injuries and lost bats, and wonders whether harnesses could help.

Wyrmbait is the 7th Legion's means of drawing Icestorm, a frostwyrm, close enough for the soldiers to bring her down. He is sent to fetch her, promising to flush her out and telling the others to be ready when she comes.

Legion Commander Tyralion serves at the 7th Legion Front in Dragonblight. He directs the effort to bring down Icestorm, a frostwyrm, and describes the Legion's long campaign against the Scourge's frostwyrms, shouting for fire to bring her down.

Junior Apothecary Lawrence complains that talk of blight has crowded out the diversity he misses. He offers a mixture for pets that he says will make them clever and strong, suggesting he enjoys experimenting beyond the camp’s usual concerns.

Chromie is an ambassador of the Bronze Dragonflight who works across the timeways. She recruits mortal allies to investigate the Infinite Dragonflight at the Bronze Dragonshrine, where a time storm bars immortals, and to protect travelers' past selves from being erased. She can lose track of when she has met someone, yet takes threats to their existence seriously. She is surprised and relieved by reports of Nozdormu when his whereabouts are unknown.

Legion Commander Yorik is a field leader coordinating the fight against the dread lich Thel'zan. He calls on an ally to bring Thel'zan's phylactery, then plans to use it to draw the lich from hiding while Legion soldiers stand ready. His public calls to steady the troops and his relief when the ally arrives show a commander focused on getting his force through a dangerous final assault.

Highlord Bolvar Fordragon leads the Alliance effort at Fordragon Hold against the Scourge at Angrathar. He insists on seeking Alexstrasza's permission before defiling ancient dragons' bones, despite frost wyrm attacks blocking his forces' advance. He values exceptional service, credits allies with keeping the campaign alive, and is willing to take the field himself. He recognizes Wintergarde Mine's strange ore in the Wrathgate and seeks a weakness in its construction.
Nozdormu, known as The Lord of Time, is a dragonkin.
Ferithos is a dragonkin who sells reagents.
Trizormu is a dragonkin who sells trade goods.
Lethecus is a dragonkin who sells general goods.
Dalormi is a dragonkin who sells wands.
Risera is a stable master whose role covers pet stabling and recovery of lost companions.
Demestrasz is the innkeeper at Wyrmrest Temple. He welcomes visitors amid the siege following Malygos's recent actions and says they may rest under the temple's protection.

npcs.name: Admiral Barean Westwind

records.text: Admiral Barean Westwind is Grand Admiral of the Scarlet Fleet. He orders High General Abbendis to kill his listener, studies them with narrowed eyes, then dismisses them as having served their purpose and threatens a future meeting in Icecrown if they survive. His lines convey command, contempt and menace.

npcs.title: Grand Admiral of the Scarlet Fleet

records.text: Wyrmrest Protectors form a repeated defensive presence at Wyrmrest Temple and use nets against nearby targets.
An undead creature encountered in the Angrathar area of the Dragonblight.

Krasus is the dragon queen's consort. He would prefer to bring Malygos back into the fold, but reluctantly accepts the other Aspects' judgment that Malygos must be stopped. He values the Spell-Weaver as a friend and fears the loss of his protection. Krasus seeks information before planning a response to trouble in the Ruby Sanctum, his flight's home, and asks Kalecgos to help visitors identify prismatic blades.
A Scourge scavenger working to unearth Galakrond, the Wastes Scavenger tosses bones at its foes.
An undead transformed warhorse in Dragonblight.
Thiassi the Lightning Bringer is an undead creature that hurls Thiassi's Stormbolt in battle.
Garmin Herzog is a stable master who discusses stabling pets and recovering lost companions.
Cid Flounderfix is a flight master associated with fast travel.

Crusader Valus is an Argent Crusader at Light's Trust who urges unity between Horde and Alliance against the Lich King. His stance toward the Scourge is severe: he calls the Drakkari they have raised lost to the Light and sends aid to Light's Breach as the Scourge pushes into Zul'Drak.
An Argent Crusader, a humanoid.
Crag Steelbeard, a named humanoid.
Montegue Krole, a humanoid in Dragonblight.
Birmingheim, a humanoid in Dragonblight.
An Argent Horseman in Dragonblight.
A Wrathgate Forsaken blightspreader wearing a gas mask.

Magister Tyr'ganal is a Kirin Tor magister who greets visitors and offers those ready to travel a teleport to Dalaran. He describes the city's move from Lordamere to above Crystalsong Forest and directs the traveler to deliver his signet to Archmage Celindra at the Violet Gate.
A humanoid Moa'ki who rides turtles.
The Warden of the Chamber is a dragonkin in Dragonblight.

During the new year and bright moon season, Elder Morthie speaks of the ancients awakening and calls it “our time.” Morthie is named among the elders visitors can ask about, including Thoim, Skywarden, Nurgen and Pamuya.

During the new year and bright moon season, Elder Thoim speaks of the ancients awakening and calls it “our time.” Thoim’s menu names Morthie, Skywarden, Nurgen and Whurain as fellow elders visitors can ask about.
Elder Skywarden recalls that in days past “we” hunted for glory and honor, then asks whether the present is so different. Skywarden’s words center on the old hunt and its meaning in the current age.
A Kor’kron battle wyvern, identified by its name with the Kor’kron war effort.
A Warsong Elite, a Horde humanoid fighter at the Wrathgate.
A Forsaken catapult, a siege engine associated with the Forsaken at the Wrathgate.
A Wrathgate Frail Construct in Dragonblight.
A Wrathgate Angrathar Aberration in Dragonblight.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Taunka huntsman on the Horde side.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Darkspear member on the Horde side.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Fordragon footman on the Alliance side.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Fordragon sentinel on the Alliance side.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Fordragon battle-mage on the Alliance side.
This Wrathgate portrayal depicts a Fordragon marksman on the Alliance side.
A Wrathgate Abomination in Dragonblight.
A Wrathgate Scourge Plague Eruptor in Dragonblight.
An unnamed fleeing Alliance soldier.
An unnamed fleeing Alliance soldier.
A fleeing Horde soldier.
A fleeing Horde soldier.

Alexstrasza, Queen of the Dragons, speaks for the red dragonflight at the Wrath Gate aftermath. She says the fallen paladin’s fate must remain undiscovered for now. She says the dragonflight has done what it can and leaves what follows to Azeroth’s mortal races. She directs Alliance and Horde heroes to recover Bolvar’s shield or Saurfang’s armor and carry the news to their leaders.
Korialstrasz is the queen's dragon consort. Addressing her as 'My Queen,' he asks whether others know and answers with the assurance, 'They will not.'
The Tempus Wyrm is a dragonkin that strikes its foes with Time Shock.
The Infinite Eradicator is a dragonkin that speeds itself with Hasten and fights with Wing Buffet and Temporal Vortex.
The Infinite Timebreaker is a dragonkin that casts Time Stop and flies into a rage when badly hurt.
Tukemuth is a rare beast that stabs with its tusks at close range and tramples its foes.
The Crazed Indu'le Survivor is a powerful humanoid who fights with Mortal Strike and goes mad when badly wounded.
Scarlet Highlord Daion is a powerful humanoid who fights with Whirlwind and turns to Bloodthirst when badly hurt.
Cielstrasza is the Wyrmrest Accord Quartermaster, a dragonkin who trades goods.
The Dragonblight Mage Hunter is a humanoid combatant that responds to spell hits with Fire Reflection.

Surveyor Hansen is promoting Venomspite’s expansion onto the Forgotten Shore and sees the beach’s potential profit. He asks for the shore to be cleared of its ghosts, shipwrecked crews and other dead, and imagines a future mausoleum or vacation spot there, which he playfully considers naming Hansen’s Cove.
Hansen’s Warhorse is a horse associated with Surveyor Hansen.
Sairuk is a Kalu’ak quartermaster who offers goods to browse.
The Dragonblight Flame Warden welcomes visitors to honor the Alliance festival flame. The Warden urges honoring fires in Alliance lands and desecrating Horde fires.
